name: Battle of Stalingrad
note: The plan shows the whole operation, not a single field: each block is an army, a corps or a pair or trio of armies, and the ground is the city and the two rivers. The accounts do not give map positions, so the places are placed by judgement to show who stood on which side of the city; north is taken as up, with the Volga to the east. Tank and mechanised armies are drawn as cavalry. The Romanian 4th Army is called the Romanian 4th Army Corps in one sentence. The Soviet northern and southern blocks are the armies of Operation Uranus; the last phases reuse them for the ring that closed in January, although the accounts do not name which armies. The part of the 62nd Army cut off on 14 October is drawn at the north by judgement; the accounts do not say where it stood.

phases.title: The 6th Army reaches Stalingrad
phases.text: The 6th Army reached the outskirts of Stalingrad in pursuit of the Soviet 62nd and 64th Armies, which fell back into the city. The 4th Panzer Army had turned northwards to help take the city from the south. Romanian armies guarded the German flanks.
phases.quote: On 23 August, the 6th Army reached the outskirts of Stalingrad in pursuit of the 62nd and 64th Armies, which had fallen back into the city.

phases.title: The attack on the city itself begins
phases.text: The German attack on the city overran the small hill where the 62nd Army headquarters stood. The railway station was captured and the Germans advanced far enough to threaten the Volga landing stage.
phases.quote: In addition, the railway station was captured, and German forces advanced far enough to threaten the Volga landing stage.

phases.title: The Germans hold the south, the Soviets the centre and north
phases.text: The Germans made slow but steady progress through the city and by 27 September held its southern part. The Soviets held the centre and the north, and with them the ferries to their supplies on the east bank of the Volga.
phases.quote: By 27 September, the Germans occupied the southern portion of the city, but the Soviets held the centre and northern part.

phases.title: The factory assault splits the 62nd Army
phases.text: After an intense bombardment the German assault groups attacked towards the Stalingrad Tractor Factory. The forward group reached the Volga, splitting the 62nd Army into two.
phases.quote: the forward assault group reached the tractor factory before arriving at the Volga River, splitting the 62nd Army into two.

phases.title: The Germans push the defenders to the river
phases.text: The Germans advanced into the city at great cost and pushed the Soviet defenders back into narrow zones along the west bank of the Volga.
phases.quote: By mid-November, the Germans, at great cost, had pushed the Soviet defenders back into narrow zones along the Volga's west bank.

phases.title: Operation Uranus overruns the Romanian 3rd Army
phases.text: Three Soviet armies struck the northern flank of the 6th Army. The Romanian 3rd Army, with thin lines and outnumbered and poorly equipped, was overrun.
phases.quote: On 19 November 1942, Operation Uranus was launched.

phases.title: A second attack comes from the south
phases.text: A second Soviet offensive of two armies was launched south of Stalingrad against the Romanian 4th Army Corps. The Romanian infantry were overrun by large numbers of tanks.
phases.quote: On 20 November, a second Soviet offensive (two armies) was launched to the south of Stalingrad against points held by the Romanian 4th Army Corps.

phases.title: The ring closes at Kalach
phases.text: The two Soviet forces raced west and met at Kalach, sealing the ring around Stalingrad. The 6th Army and the 4th Panzer Army were left inside it.
phases.quote: The Soviet forces raced west and met on 23 November at the town of Kalach, sealing the ring around Stalingrad.

phases.title: The relief force advances from Kotelnikovo
phases.text: Operation Winter Storm was left with the LVII Panzer Corps around Kotelnikovo, supported by the rest of the 4th Panzer Army. By 18 December it had pushed to within 48 km of the 6th Army. The trapped army made no attempt to break out or link up.
phases.quote: By 18 December, the German Army had pushed to within 48 km (30 mi)

phases.title: The relief attempt is abandoned
phases.text: The attempt to relieve Stalingrad was given up. Manstein's forces, including the LVII Panzer Corps, switched to the defensive.
phases.quote: On 23 December, the attempt to relieve Stalingrad was abandoned, and Manstein's forces switched over to the defensive

phases.title: Operation Koltso begins
phases.text: Operation Koltso opened on 10 January 1943 with a very large bombardment of the German positions. The Germans retreated from the suburbs of Stalingrad to the city.
phases.quote: Operation Koltso launched on 10 January 1943 with what was the single largest bombardment of the war at that point

phases.title: The German forces are split into two pockets
phases.text: The German forces inside Stalingrad were split into two pockets, one north and one south of Mamayev Kurgan. The northern pocket was cut off from telephone communication with Paulus in the southern pocket.
phases.quote: On 26 January, the German forces inside Stalingrad were split into two pockets north and south of Mamayev Kurgan

phases.title: The southern and central pockets collapse
phases.text: The southern pocket collapsed on 31 January, and the central pocket under Heitz surrendered the same day. The northern pocket under Strecker held out for two more days.
phases.quote: The next day, the southern pocket in Stalingrad collapsed.

phases.title: The northern pocket surrenders
phases.text: On 2 February General Strecker learned that one of his officers had gone to the Soviets to negotiate terms, and the northern pocket surrendered. The 6th Army, having exhausted its ammunition and food, had capitulated.
phases.quote: On 2 February 1943, the 6th Army, having exhausted its ammunition and food, finally capitulated
